why: A varies the shape of every section - a photographic hero with a captioned overlay, a real client-logo row, a working quote form, a bespoke drawn route map, one dark full-bleed band, an accordion - while B runs the same two modules (a four-card grid and a numbered list of rows) around six times under alternating blue and white bands. A's hierarchy survives desaturation because it is built from scale and value contrast: the hero type is far larger than the body, the dark step band changes the page's weight, the photos anchor two sections; in B the only thing separating a heading from its body copy is a small size step, so each band reads as one flat slab and the structure is carried entirely by the band colour. A's imagery is specific and owned - a branded trailer, the actual Danone, Shin-Line and Hamle marks - where B's trust row is the client names typeset inside empty outlined boxes, which reads as a logo wall nobody ever supplied logos for.
loser_fatal_flaw: Hierarchy is colour-only. Strip the blue bands and B collapses into an undifferentiated column of small text - headings, labels, list rows and body all sit at nearly the same weight and size, so nothing tells the eye where a section starts or what matters inside it.
winner_worst_flaw: The hero stacks two competing headlines - a question and a claim - in two different colours, so the page opens without a single sentence in charge, and the pale-blue-on-white upper third gives that spread almost no value contrast to sit against.
ai_evidence: Sequential 01-07 chips marking every section, the signature of a generated section inventory rather than an argued page
Client names set as plain text inside empty outlined boxes where real logos belong
The same four-card grid reused for what we take on, our fleet and why choose us, with only the labels changed
Numbered five-to-six-row lists used for services, geography and process alike, so three unrelated ideas get one form
A complete section-title checklist - services, geography, trust, why us, how we work, contact - covering every generic B2B heading in order
The footer restates the entire top navigation and both CTA buttons verbatim
Two truck photographs from visibly different fleets and cropped to different logics, placed as decoration rather than evidence
